changes.reason: Lines 36-37: acquainted with all the principal people, lively and unreserved, at the ball. Lines 7-8: from an upper window, blue coat and black horse. Stock sentence gone; wrong-scope described.
Line 29: ten thousand a year is Mr Darcy's, carried to Mr Bingley (attribute transfer). Lines 7-8 upper window, blue coat, black horse. Stock sentence gone.
Line 8: the black horse is the one Mr Bingley rode, carried across to Mr Bennet (attribute transfer). Lines 5-6: hopes of a sight of the young ladies. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 15-17: Lady Lucas starts the idea of his going to London for a large party, after the refusal. Line 11: obliged to be in town the following day. Stock sentence gone.
Line 18: twelve ladies, and the girls grieved (18-19), outside lines 13-16. Lines 14-15: she began to fear he might always be flying about and never settled at Netherfield. Stock sentence gone.
Line 38: talked of giving one himself at Netherfield, later in the passage. Lines 21-22: the party that entered the assembly-room consisted of only five. Stock sentence gone.

Line 37: Bingley danced every dance. Lines 39-40: Darcy danced only once with Mrs Hurst and once with Miss Bingley. Lines 27-29: fine, tall person, handsome features, report of ten thousand a year. Stock sentence gone.
Line 33: the Derbyshire estate is outside lines 26-30 and named after his manners turned the tide (31-32). Lines 27-29 give looks and ten thousand a year. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 37-38: Bingley angry that the ball closed so early. Lines 31-32: his manners gave a disgust; discovered to be proud, above his company. Stock sentence gone.

Line 37: every dance is Bingley's, just before the window at 39. Lines 39-40: Darcy danced only once with Mrs Hurst and once with Miss Bingley. Stock sentence gone (and the old false 'one line above' is corrected).
Lines 55-56: Darcy's reply, a punishment to stand up with any other woman. Quote 'I must have you dance.' is exact at line 51. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 4-5: the wind blew the dry leaves across the road in a shower, at the start of the journey. Lines 23-24: an oak, torn up by the roots, fell across the road. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 34-35: the mark he had made on the wall. Line 38: he would take the rule, and re-measure. Stock sentence gone; wrong-scope described.
Line 4: quote 'Wake up! wake up!' exact, said by Roberta, after Phyllis's 'Wassermarrer?' at line 3. Line 1: woke Phyllis by pulling her hair gently. Stock sentence gone.
Line 24: 'I did not dare, because I was staying in the house', about laughing at the reading (line 23). Line 50: 'It is said' is exact. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 14-15: her mother deposited a bundle and a bouquet of lilacs beside her before setting off. Line 50: 'there ain't no extry charge to sit side o' me'. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 30-31: Mark at once went round, hastening to get in front. Bevis never asks for this anywhere in the passage. Line 1: 'Go and fetch my fishing-rod'. Stock sentence gone.
Line 10: Stuart opens the 'grown smaller' argument and Ralph answers at 11; that is four lines past line 6. Line 3: Ralph, 'No country is safe for him.' Stock sentence gone.

'Fogg answers it at line 23 with All included rather than correcting it' is false. At lines 20-22 Stuart claims the eighty days does not take bad weather into account. Fogg's 'All included' (line 23) flatly contradicts that, which is a correction. The out-of-window point is all the execution needs, and that is true: weather is at line 21, outside lines 16-19. Line 18 'three months' and line 19 'In eighty days' are quoted exactly. Fix: drop 'rather than correcting it' and say the correction about weather comes at line 23, outside the window.
Line 42: Stuart wagers the four thousand, three lines before line 45. Lines 45-46: Fogg's deposit of twenty thousand at Baring's. Stock sentence gone.
Line 6: 'goes by the post and Kieran swears it was in' is quoted exactly. Line 31 gives their end proper netting; line 33 gives ours two jumpers. Stock sentence gone.
Line 32: climbed up in the big man's lap to see how writing was done. Lines 5-6: scratch himself anywhere he pleased with any leg. Stock sentence gone.
Lines 7-8: 'every year they go over in the wind', said of Denise's dahlias. Line 13: the tomato leaves had curled in on themselves and gone crisp. Stock sentence gone.
Line 23: he counted them (the potatoes) into the bucket out loud. Lines 35-36: got through half of his and passed me the rest. Stock sentence gone.

rows.reason: Lines 5-8: the key (coat and horse colour) is the only thing ascertained from the window. Ten minutes (line 4), cheerful (36-37), ten thousand (29, Darcy's) and liking the house (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 5-6: hopes of a sight of the young ladies. Book (unstated), invitation reversed (lines 9-12, the Bennets'), horse (line 8, Bingley's own) and dance (60-61, later) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 11: obliged to be in town (London, line 16) the following day. Lady Lucas, motive, courses (9-10, Mrs Bennet's) and London party (15-17) all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 14-15: fear of his flying about and never settled at Netherfield. Cooked dinner (unstated), Lady Lucas's idea (16-17), twelve ladies (18) and dislike (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 21-22: 'party' is the five who entered together. Dominant sense, political sense, the Netherfield ball (38) and everyone at the assembly (wrong value) all fail. Executions are true.

Both redrafts are attested, but an unredrafted execution on this row is false. On 'Because he spoke kindly to everyone he was introduced to' it reads 'line 40 has him decline being introduced to anyone'. Lines 40-41 say he 'declined being introduced to any other lady'. Line 42 also has him speaking occasionally to his own party. Fix: 'declined being introduced to any other lady'. Key, stem and the other distractors check against lines 26-30.

Lines 31-32: his manners, proud and above his company. Not rich (33 still a large estate), looks (34-35 the result, not the cause), Bingley's complaint (37-38) and 'from the moment he walked in' (30-31 admired half the evening) all fail. Executions are true.

The 'Every dance' redraft is attested, but the execution on 'Three: with Mrs Hurst, Miss Bingley and Miss Bennet' says 'she dances with Mr Bingley at line 63'. Line 63 is about Elizabeth sitting down behind Darcy. Mr Bingley's dance with the eldest Miss Bennet is at lines 60-61 ('You are dancing with the only handsome girl in the room ... the eldest Miss Bennet'). Fix: lines 60 and 61. The key and the other distractors check against lines 39-40.
Line 51: 'I must have you dance.' Stem quote is exact at lines 51-52. Rudeness (55-56, Darcy's reply), going home and pity for ladies all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 23-24: an oak torn up by the roots falls across the road. Branch (John's worry, line 20), bridge (47) and leaves (4-5) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 38: he takes the rule and re-measures, so it is a measuring tool. Law (dominant sense), mark on the wall (34-35) and 'as a rule' (neighbouring sense) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 1: woke Phyllis by pulling her hair gently. Shouting (line 4, after she stirs), blankets (unstated) and the reversal all fail. Executions are true.

Line 50: 'It is said' (and 'If he did', line 51) puts the report at second hand. Sympathy (unstated), not daring (24, about laughing) and penitence (51, what he did next) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 50: no extra charge to sit by him; the fare is already paid at line 16. Bundle and lilacs (14), the front seat (51, what she gets) and reins (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 1: 'Go and fetch my fishing-rod'. Watching (line 3, Mark's offer), going round (30-31, Mark's own act) and keeping quiet (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.

Lines 3-6: whether the thief has anywhere to go ('No country is safe' / 'The world is big enough'). Shrewd fellow (1-2), the world shrinking (from line 10) and England (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.

Row as it will be carries the refused redraft on 'Whether bad weather has been taken into account'. The claim that Fogg answers it 'rather than correcting it' is false: line 23 'All included' contradicts Stuart's claim at lines 20-22. If the redraft does not land, the old stock sentence stays. The key (line 18 'three months', corrected at 19 'In eighty days') and the other distractors check.

Lines 45-46: Fogg's twenty thousand deposited at Baring's. Least possible time (50-51, the objector's), four thousand (42, Stuart's) and everything he owns (74, half his fortune) all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 31 and 33: netting against two jumpers. Date (32), post (6) and width (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.
Lines 5-6: scratch himself anywhere he pleased with any leg. Tail (6, not a leg), lap (32) and running faster (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.
Line 13: curled in on themselves and gone crisp. Soak (14, what he did), going over in the wind (7-8, dahlias) and the open door (unstated) all fail. Executions are true.

Lines 35-36: got through half and passed me the rest. Enormous breakfast (36, what he said), counting (23, potatoes) and keeping them back (unstated; 35 gives one o'clock) all fail. Executions are true.
